Option A ("Typing speed") fails because it confuses literacy with motor skill; Option C ("Device repair") fails because it confuses literacy with hardware; Option D ("Source verification") fails because it confuses literacy with checking sources.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Why length beats complexity in a password
questions.learningObjective: Explain why length matters more than complexity

stimulus.body: Dans une note de travail consacrée à ce point, on lit: «Length increases the number of possible combinations more.» Quatre affirmations sont proposées; une seule est conforme à ce que la note établit réellement.

questions.stem: Avec l’indice «Length grows combinations.», quelle option est réellement appuyée par le texte ?

options.text: Short passwords are easier to remember.
Length increases the number of possible combinations more.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: length grows the search space more effectively. On that basis "Length increases the number of possible combinations more" is the supported choice. Option A ("Short passwords are easier to remember") fails because it confuses memorability with security; Option B ("Complexity is always useless") fails because it overstates the point; Option D ("Complex passwords are illegal") fails because it invents a false rule.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What open public wifi exposes

stimulus.body: Contexte du texte : «It exposes your traffic to others on the network.» A traveller uses open wifi in an airport to read the news. The network has no password. L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: Le passage est confronté à «Explain what public wifi exposes / Open networks expose traffic. / What open public wifi exposes». Quelle réponse résiste ?

options.text: It exposes your traffic to others on the network.
It exposes only your device's colour.
It exposes nothing if you are quick.
It exposes only the airport's schedule.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: b trivialises, C confuses speed with safety, and D confuses network with airport. On that basis "It exposes your traffic to others on the network" is the supported choice. Option B ("It exposes only your device's colour") fails because it trivialises the risk; Option C ("It exposes nothing if you are quick") fails because it confuses speed with safety; Option D ("It exposes only the airport's schedule") fails because it confuses network with airport.

It limits who can see the post.
